ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In the rectangular region I, there exists a uniform magnetic field with magnetic induction strength $B$ perpendicular to the plane of the paper and pointing outward. The lines $aa'$ and $b b^{\prime}$ are mutually parallel boundaries of the magnetic field, and the length of the rectangular magnetic field region is sufficiently long, with a width of $L$. A certain type of positively charged particle enters the magnetic field in region I from point $O_{I}$ on $a a^{\prime}$ at different velocities, moving in a direction that forms an angle $\alpha{=}30^{\circ}$ with $O_{I}a$. The mass of the charged particle is $m$, and its charge is $+q$. The interactions between charged particles are neglected, and the gravitational force on the charged particle is not considered.

1. What is the magnitude of the velocity \( v_{I} \) such that a particle incident at this velocity just cannot exit region I from the right side?
2. What is the time \( t \) for a particle incident at a rate \( v_{2} \) (where \( v_{2} \) is less than the \( v_{I} \) obtained in part (1)) to move within region I?
3. What is the magnitude of the velocity \( v_{3} \) if the time taken for a particle moving at velocity \( v_{3} \) to travel through region I is \( \frac{1}{5} \) of the time \( t \) obtained in question (2)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$v_{1}=\frac{2q B L}{(2+\sqrt{3})m}$
$t=\frac{5\pi m}{3q B}$
$v_{3}=\frac{2\sqrt{3}q B L}{3m}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a long and narrow rectangular magnetic field region I; the left and right boundaries are respectively the vertical straight lines aa′ and bb′, and the two boundaries are parallel to each other; black dots in the region indicate that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface outward. On the left boundary aa′ there is an incident point O_I; the velocity direction of the particle entering from O_I is obliquely upward to the right, and it makes an angle α with the upward direction O_Ia along aa′. In the figure, a horizontal dashed line points from O_I to the right boundary, and the distance between the two vertical boundaries is marked as L at the bottom. Reasoning: Take O_I as the origin, the x-axis horizontally to the right pointing to bb′, and the y-axis upward along aa′. A positive charge, under the action of the Lorentz force in a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the paper surface outward, makes clockwise circular motion, with angular velocity ω=qB/m and orbital radius R=mv/(qB). The initial velocity makes an angle α with the vertical direction, so the coordinates of the circle center relative to O_I are C=(R cosα, -R sinα). 1. When the particle “just cannot exit from the right side,” the rightmost end of the circular orbit is exactly tangent to the right boundary bb′, that is, the maximum value of x is equal to L: R cosα+R=L, so R(1+cosα)=L. Substituting α=30°, cos30°=√3/2, gives R=2L/(2+√3). From R=mv_I/(qB), we get v_I=2qBL/[(2+√3)m]. 2. If v_2<v_I, then R is smaller, the rightmost end of the orbit cannot reach the right boundary bb′, and the particle will leave the magnetic field again from the left boundary aa′. The radius directions corresponding to the two intersection points of the circle and x=0 are respectively vertically symmetric on the left side with respect to the circle center; from the incident point to reaching x=0 again, the central angle swept by the particle in the clockwise direction is 2π-2α. α=30°=π/6, so the swept angle is 2π-π/3=5π/3. Therefore the motion time in the magnetic field is t=(5π/3)/ω=5πm/(3qB). 3. If, when the speed is v_3, the time to pass through region I is 1/5 of t in the previous question, then its motion time is t/5=πm/(3qB), corresponding to a swept central angle of ω(t/5)=π/3. After the initial radius vector rotates clockwise by π/3 around the circle center, it reaches the right boundary x=L. Using the circle center coordinates C=(R cosα,-R sinα), substituting α=30° and rotation angle π/3, the abscissa of the arrival point is obtained as L=R cos30°. Therefore R=L/cos30°=2L/√3. From v_3=qBR/m, we get v_3=2qBL/(√3 m)=2√3qBL/(3m).
